item.title: Artemis I: Crystals of experimental detectors record radiation doses near the moon
item.description: Do cosmic radiation doses near the moon differ significantly from those received by astronauts in low Earth orbit? Experimental lithium fluoride detectors, installed aboard the Orion spacecraft during the Artemis I mission, have now made it possible to obtain preliminary estimates.

item.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
item.description: The Martian Moons eXploration ( MMX ) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. item.title: Rare Lunar Meteorites Could Fill Gaps In Moon’s Evolution
item.description: Almost all meteorites come from asteroids, not the Moon or Mars. But after decades of analysis of the Apollo samples, researchers still rely on lunar meteorites to better understand our anomalously large Moon.

item.title: Everyday Mylar turned into a promising insulator for lunar habitats
item.description: Establishing a long-term presence on the moon will require solving challenges that are easy to overlook on Earth. Lunar temperatures, for instance, can vary from hundreds of degrees below zero to boiling, making effective insulation essential for lunar habitats.

item.title: Pedal to the metal: NASA's Psyche heads toward asteroid belt
item.description: With a successful Mars gravity assist in its rearview mirror, NASA's Psyche spacecraft has fired up its thrusters and is accelerating toward the metal-rich asteroid of the same name. During the first leg of its journey, following an October 2023 launch, the mission used its electric propulsion system intermittently to maneuver into the right position to harness Mars' gravity for a propellant-saving speed boost and a slight trajectory change.

item.title: Euclid discovers new comet
item.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.

item.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
item.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express , in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.

item.title: Lincoln Laboratory laser communications terminal launches on historic Artemis II moon mission
item.description: High-definition video and data sent from the lunar vicinity to Earth will demonstrate the first use of laser communications on a crewed mission.

item.title: Study: Rocks from Mars’ Jezero Crater, which likely predate life on Earth, contain signs of water
item.description: The presence of organic matter is inconclusive, but the rocks could be scientists’ best chance at finding remnants of ancient Martian life.

item.title: Study determines the original orientations of rocks drilled on Mars
item.description: The “oriented” samples, the first of their kind from any planet, could shed light on Mars’ ancient magnetic field.

item.title: Fly around Schiaparelli Crater with Mars Express
item.description: Video: 00:04:10 ESA’s Mars Express takes us on another mesmerising flight, this time around one of the biggest craters on Mars. Despite measuring a huge 460 km across, Schiaparelli Crater seems to be relatively shallow. Perhaps it has been filled in over the last few billion years by sediment blown by the wind or deposited by water, by lava – or by a combination of all three. item.title: Scientists pin down the origins of the moon’s tenuous atmosphere
item.description: The barely-there lunar atmosphere is likely the product of meteorite impacts over billions of years, a new study finds.
